Heat a pan or wok over high heat. Sear beef in batches for 2-3 minutes until browned and slightly charred, leaving it untouched for about 1 minute before flipping. Remove from pan.
Add oil, then garlic and ginger paste. Stir-fry 1-2 minutes until fragrant. Add Chinese broccoli stems and cook 2 minutes, then add the leaves and cook 1-2 minutes until wilted. Remove from pan.
Add noodles to the hot pan and let sit undisturbed for about 30 seconds to lightly char. Toss gently so they don't break apart. Pour in the sauce and cook 1 minute until evenly coated.
Return beef and vegetables to the pan and toss 1-2 minutes until glossy and combined. Add bean sprouts and spring onions during the last 30 seconds.
Serve immediately, hot.
imageCredit: Illustrative photo from Red House Spice (redhousespice.com) — not a photo of this exact recipe

name: Quick Beef Curry (Kids)
timeNote: Cook time is 30 min, 35 min total with prep — a touch over the 30-min cap if you count prep.
note: Kids version of the adult Quick Beef Curry. De-spiced by dropping the fresh chilli entirely and halving the garam masala for a gentler bite — the cardamom, cumin, coriander and turmeric are kept since they're warming spices, not heat. Calories land right in the 475-500 kcal target without any other portion changes.
steps: Add cumin seeds, coriander seeds and cardamom pods to the TM bowl. Roast 5 min/Varoma/Speed 1 (MC out).
Mill 1 min/Speed 10.
Scrape down bowl. Add onion, ginger, garlic. Chop 10 sec/Speed 5.
Scrape down bowl. Add oil and turmeric. Sauté 5 min/Varoma/Speed 2 (MC out).
Add stock, tomato paste, yoghurt and beef. Cook 25 min/Varoma/Speed 1 (Reverse Blade).
Add garam masala and kasoori methi. Cook 1 min/Varoma/Speed 1 (Reverse Blade). Serve.

name: Kerabu Taugeh (Bean Sprout Salad)
note: Source publishes no nutrition data — calories/macros are my own estimate from the ingredient list. Doubled from the as-written recipe to make 2 snack-sized servings.
steps: Combine all ingredients in a bowl.
Toss and serve immediately.

name: Restaurant-Style Edamame
steps: Bring a pot of salted water to a rolling boil, filling the pot roughly three-quarters full.
Add the frozen edamame and cook for 5 minutes.
Strain the edamame and sprinkle with salt.
Serve warm with extra salt if desired (only eat the beans inside the pods).

name: Simple Shio Onigiri
timeNote: Assumes rice is already cooked and cooled ahead of time (standard for batch prep) — this is just the shaping/wrapping time.
note: Scaled to a 2-rice-ball portion (one per person) from the source's 6-ball batch. Protein/fat/carbs are my estimate — source only publishes calories per ball.
steps: Set up a bowl of ice water, the salt, and the cooked rice.
Wash hands thoroughly and dip fingertips in the ice-cold water for 15-20 seconds.
Rub a pinch of salt over both palms.
Take a handful of warm rice and shape using the "press and turn" technique into a triangle. Repeat for the second ball.
Wrap each onigiri with a strip of nori.
Eat immediately, or pack in a lunch box with an ice pack.

name: Cucumber Bites (Whipped Feta)
note: Scaled to a 2-serving (1/4-batch) portion from the source's 8-serving recipe.
steps: In a small bowl or food processor, combine feta, lemon juice and zest, honey, and dill; blend until smooth (a fork-mash works fine for a small batch).
Stream in olive oil while mixing until completely smooth.
Spoon a dollop of whipped feta onto each cucumber slice.
Garnish with fresh dill and pepper; serve.

name: Cold-Tossed Tofu (凉拌豆腐)
note: Scaled to a 2-serving (half-batch) portion from the source's 4-serving recipe. Best assembled fresh — refrigerate up to 1 day before the onion/cilantro start releasing water and softening the texture.
steps: In a bowl, combine minced garlic, soy sauce, chili oil (if using), sesame oil, sugar and white pepper. Mix until sugar dissolves.
Add cubed tofu, red onion and cilantro. Gently toss until combined.
Serve immediately, or refrigerate up to 1 day before serving.

name: Five-Spice Edamame (五香毛豆)
timeNote: 3 min prep + 7 min active cook; there's also a 4hr-to-overnight passive soak in the spiced brine before serving — plan ahead.
note: Scaled to a 2-serving (half-batch) portion from the source's 4-serving recipe. Source notes its nutrition figures are auto-calculated and approximate.
steps: Trim the stem ends of the edamame pods with scissors so the flavor can penetrate.
Bring water to a boil, add edamame and salt. Once boiling resumes, simmer 2 minutes.
Transfer edamame to cold water with a slotted spoon; keep the hot cooking water.
Add ginger, star anise, cinnamon, Sichuan pepper, bay leaf and chilies to the hot water. Simmer 5 minutes on low heat, then cool 20 minutes.
Drain the edamame and pour the spiced water over them. Soak 4 hours, or overnight, before serving.

name: Corn Chaat
timeNote: Uses the frozen-corn sauté method (not the boiled-fresh-corn version) to stay at ~8-10 min active — sautéing thawed corn in butter for 2-3 min instead of boiling.
steps: Sauté thawed corn kernels in butter over medium heat for 2-3 minutes until just tender.
Cool slightly, then mix in chili powder, cumin powder, chaat masala and salt.
Fold in onion, tomato, green chili, lemon juice and coriander leaves.
Transfer to bowls and top with sev, farsan or roasted peanuts.

name: Kala Chana Chaat
timeNote: Only the daily-assembly step (chopping + tossing) is ≤10 min — the chickpeas need an overnight soak plus a 25-40 min pressure-cook as a separate batch step done once ahead of time.
note: Scaled to a 2-serving (half-batch) portion from the source's 4-serving recipe.
steps: Soak dried black chickpeas overnight (or at least 4 hours) in water; drain and rinse.
Pressure-cook (Instant Pot: high pressure 25 min if soaked overnight; stovetop: 7-8 whistles), natural release; drain.
Add the cooked chickpeas to a bowl with the chopped tomato, onion, cilantro and mint.
Mix in chaat masala, kala namak, cumin powder, amchur and red chili powder.
Toss, squeeze over the lime juice, and serve chilled.

name: No Bake Energy Balls
timeNote: 10 min active mixing/rolling; there's also a 30 min passive fridge chill before rolling (no hands-on work during that time).
note: Scaled to a 2-ball portion (one per person) from the source's 16-ball batch. Protein/fat/carbs are my estimate — source only publishes calories per ball.
steps: Combine all ingredients in a bowl and stir until well blended.
Refrigerate the mixture for 30 minutes.
Roll into 2 balls (about 1 tbsp each).
Store in an airtight container in the refrigerator or freezer.

name: Smoked Salmon Cucumber Bites
note: The only non-vegetarian Snack (pescatarian — contains smoked salmon). Source publishes 22 kcal/bite; a 6-bite portion (~132 kcal) is defined as 1 serving here to land in the 100-200 kcal snack target. Protein/fat/carbs are my estimate — source only publishes calories per bite.
steps: Whip cream cheese, lemon juice, garlic, half the chives, salt and pepper together until smooth.
Spread onto cucumber rounds; top each with a piece of smoked salmon.
Garnish with remaining chives, plus extra salt and pepper.
Refrigerate leftovers, covered, and use within a couple of days.

name: Otak-Otak (Nyonya Fish Cake)
timeNote: ~10 min active (blending, wrapping) + ~10 min passive steaming.
note: Source publishes no nutrition data — calories are my estimate, with real uncertainty (~185-260 kcal/serving) depending on cooking method and how much oil is used. Steaming (the method used here) keeps it toward the lower/middle of that range. Scaled to a 2-serving portion from the source's 6-serving batch.
steps: Remove skin and bones from mackerel; set the meat aside.
Combine mackerel, coconut milk, red curry paste, cornstarch and oil in a food processor; blend until smooth.
Clean banana leaves and cut to size. Place spoonfuls of the paste on the dull side of the leaf; wrap and secure with toothpicks.
Steam over boiling water for about 10 minutes until set (or grill/bake — steaming is the most hands-off option).

name: Kacang Rebus (Boiled Peanuts)
timeNote: ~5-10 min active (rinsing, assembling, occasional stirring) + ~25 min passive simmer/soak.
note: The source's own published figure (90 kcal/100g) looks inconsistent with USDA data for boiled peanuts (~318 kcal/100g) — used the USDA-based figure instead, which is more defensible. Portioned at 110g shelled peanuts per person to land at the top of the hearty band.

ingredients.n: Pandan leaves, tied in a knot

steps: Rinse raw peanuts (in shell) thoroughly; discard any damaged ones.
Bring water to a boil in a large pot.
Add peanuts with pandan leaves, lemongrass, salt, garlic, bay leaf, turmeric and chili (if using).
Cover and simmer 20 minutes on medium heat, stirring occasionally, topping up water as needed.
Test a peanut for tenderness; adjust salt to taste.
Turn off heat, let soak 5 minutes.
Drain, discard the aromatics, shell the peanuts and serve warm (or refrigerate for batch prep).

name: Tamago Sando (Japanese Egg Sandwich)
timeNote: ~10 min active (boiling water, peeling, mashing, mixing, buttering, assembling, cutting); ~17 min passive (12 min egg boil + 5 min plate-press).
steps: Boil eggs in water for 12 minutes, then transfer to an ice bath until cooled.
Peel and mash eggs with a fork into uniform pieces.
Mix mashed eggs with sugar, salt and pepper.
Add milk and Kewpie mayonnaise; blend thoroughly.
Spread salted butter on all 4 bread slices.
Distribute egg salad on two slices; top with the remaining buttered slices (buttered side down).
Compress sandwiches between plates for 5 minutes.
Remove crusts and cut sandwiches diagonally.

name: Teriyaki Tofu
timeNote: ~12-14 min active (cutting, coating, pan-frying both sides, reducing the sauce) — a touch over 10 min. Draining the tofu (20-30 min, or ~2-3 min if microwaved) is passive/prep-ahead.
note: Bonito flakes (katsuobushi) omitted here to keep this vegetarian, per the source's own suggested substitution.

ingredients.n: Teriyaki sauce (2 tbsp each sake, mirin, soy sauce)
Green onion, sliced & pickled red ginger (garnish)

steps: Drain tofu by wrapping in paper towel between two plates with a weight, 20-30 minutes (or microwave 2-3 minutes as a shortcut).
Combine sake, mirin and soy sauce in a measuring cup.
Cut drained tofu lengthwise in half, then crosswise into ½-inch slabs.
Slice green onion; heat oil in a nonstick pan over medium-high heat.
Coat tofu pieces with potato starch, shaking off excess.
Pan-fry until golden, 3-5 minutes per side.
Pour in the teriyaki sauce; shake/flip tofu to coat evenly until the sauce thickens.
Transfer to a plate; garnish with green onion and pickled ginger.

name: Greek Yogurt with Honey and Walnuts
timeNote: ~2-3 min active (portioning yogurt, mixing) + ~8 min passive walnut-toasting (can happen while you portion the yogurt).
note: Scaled to a 2-serving portion from the source's 7-serving batch.
steps: Preheat oven to 180°C. Spread walnuts on a baking sheet and toast 7-8 minutes until golden and fragrant. Transfer to a bowl, add honey, toss to coat, let cool 1-2 minutes.
Mix Greek yogurt with vanilla extract; divide between 2 bowls.
Spoon the honey-walnut mixture over the yogurt and sprinkle with cinnamon.
Serve immediately, or refrigerate.

name: Air Fryer Chicken Tikka Bites
timeNote: ~10 min active (cutting, mixing marinade, coating) is right at the bar; plus a 15 min passive marinate and 9-12 min mostly-passive air-fry (one flip).
steps: Cut chicken into 1.5-inch cubes.
Whisk yogurt and besan together, removing lumps.
Add ginger, garlic, beet, cayenne, garam masala and salt; mix well.
Add chicken and coat completely; refrigerate at least 15 minutes.
Preheat air fryer to 190°C (380°F).
Spray air fryer tray; add chicken with spacing between pieces.
Cook 9-12 minutes, turning once after 5 minutes.

name: Turkey and Cheese Roll Ups
note: Scaled to a 2-serving (2-wrap) portion; source only publishes calories (per-serving macros beyond that are my estimate).
steps: Place a tortilla on a flat surface; layer with cheese, turkey, cucumber slices and lettuce.
Starting from one edge, tightly roll the tortilla into a log shape.
Slice into 1-inch-thick pieces with a sharp knife.
Repeat with the second tortilla; serve.
